newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen range-bound, moving narrowly.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen range-bound, moving narrowly.

text.p: The benchmark June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to be range-bound and to move relatively narrowly on Tuesday ahead of an impending benchmark shift, traders said.

The market is expecting the benchmark to change from June to September as early as Tuesday or Wednesday, something that is likely to prompt sales of June and buying of September late in the day, as happened on Monday, a trader at a securities firm said. "If the June manages to break above Monday's high of 124.37, we could see more gains, but this seems unlikely today," he said.

Sentiment carried over from overseas trade is likely to undercut futures' strength early in the day and prompt sales, although the downside is expected to be supported on reduced expectations of an early Japanese rate hike.
Some expectations of longer-term bond strength and the chances of a summer rally are also likely to prevent any sharp slides, traders said.
But with activity limited primarily to short-term buying and selling amid an absence of fresh factors, turnover is likely to be relatively good even if the range remains narrow, they said.
